title: Manjushri visits
hookLine: the bodhisattva of wisdom goes; the room holds countless seats
tomorrow: I'm sick because the world is sick

cards: Finally the Buddha turns to Manjushri, the bodhisattva of wisdom. Manjushri doesn't pretend it will be easy. Vimalakirti is hard to answer, he says; he sees deep into the teaching, and his speech is quick.
But I'll go. The moment he agrees, the whole assembly wants to come along: bodhisattvas, disciples, gods. Two great minds in one sickroom; nobody wants to miss that.
So a vast crowd follows Manjushri into the city, toward one small house.

teach.b: Vimalakirti sees them coming and does something strange. By his power he empties his house. The attendants go, the furniture goes, and nothing is left but the one bed he lies on.
Manjushri walks in, and Vimalakirti greets him with a riddle. Welcome, Manjushri.
You've come without coming, and you appear without being seen. Manjushri answers in kind: so it is. What has already come doesn't come again, and what has gone doesn't go again.

They're talking about emptiness before anyone has sat down. And nobody can sit down. A little later in the visit, Shariputra looks around the bare room and wonders where all these people are supposed to sit.
Vimalakirti reads his thought and teases him.

Did you come here for the teaching, or for a chair? Then he solves it anyway. He asks Manjushri where the finest lion thrones in all the worlds are found, and Manjushri names a Buddha in a far-off world.

teach.h: LION THRONES IN A SMALL ROOM.
teach.b: Vimalakirti calls for those thrones, and they arrive, enormous, towering, and fit into his small room without crowding it. The city outside isn't crowded either.
The bodhisattvas grow tall enough to take their seats; the disciples can't climb up until they bow to the Buddha the thrones came from. The sutra calls this kind of thing an inconceivable liberation.
The house didn't get bigger on the outside.

how: Across Mahayana traditions Manjushri is honored as the bodhisattva of wisdom, shown in images with a sword and a book, and the meeting of Manjushri and Vimalakirti appears in East Asian painting and teaching.

the bodhisattva of wisdom going where the disciples wouldn't

games.q: you're Vimalakirti. a vast crowd is walking toward your small house. what do you do?
o: empty it, until only your bed is left.
send word that you're too ill for guests.
games.why: he empties the house by his power, then later fills it with lion thrones from another world, and nothing is crowded.

practice: Notice the space you're in: the walls, the ceiling, the air between. Breathe out slowly and feel the chest make room for the next breath without being asked.
Then let in one person or one feeling you've been keeping outside, and give it a seat, the way that small room held the thrones.

wordCard.voice: Manjushri visits. The bodhisattva of wisdom goes where the disciples wouldn't, and a bare sickroom holds the whole assembly. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Manjushri, the bodhisattva of wisdom, who agrees to visit Vimalakirti.

carryVoice: Your line: the room grows. Nothing had to be squeezed to fit. See you tomorrow.
